chapter: Mamie Smith and the New York dance bands
title: Mamie Smith compared with Bessie, Clara and Trixie Smith
summary: Mamie was a smooth vaudeville singer who looked the part, not a blues shouter, and her fame owed to the first record and her agent.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Yeah, I see. Well, on -- she was hot at this time, was she?

She was tops at that time, because, you know, they had three different Smith, and neither one of the four were ever related, but Mamie, Bessie -- of course, Bessie was the tops. There was Clara Smith. There was Trixie Smith.
Well, actually Mamie was almost the least good singer, woudn't you say?
Yes, she had -- because she couldn't sing the blues up to what Bessie could.
Clara, that's right. But she sang on a smooth level, you know. She wasn't a shouter.
Well, it was good for theaters.
It was good for theaters, you know. Then vaudeville was -- Russian sable coats and all that. And she had -- she looked the part.
Well, what -- I mean was it that sort of fact that she made that record before anybody else that sort of set her off?
Because, you know, when you listen to the records she made, you can't see any reason why she should have been such a big smash as she was.
Right. I think her publicity -- I think her agent was the cause of that. Yeah, I think that's what it really was.
